pull_request.title: feat: implement require_auth_in_loop lint (Closes #6)
pull_request.body:
## Summary

Adds a new `require_auth_in_loop` lint (default severity: **warn**) that detects `Address::require_auth()` and `Address::require_auth_for_args()` calls inside loop bodies (`for`, `while`, or `loop`). The lint recommends hoisting authorization out of the loop — collecting distinct addresses and authorizing each one once before the loop — and warns that legitimate cases iterating over distinct addresses per iteration can be suppressed with `#[allow(require_auth_in_loop)]` at the call site.

## Cost rationale

`Address::require_auth` (and its `require_auth_for_args` variant) is a host-side authorization check that traverses the auth tree, verifies signatures against the matching `require_auth` records previously installed by the contract, and accounts for them in the CPU budget. It is comparatively expensive — more so than a typical in-loop mutation — and re-running it on every iteration multiplies the cost by the loop count, even when the same address is being re-authorized on every iteration.

In almost all real-world Soroban contracts, the set of addresses that need authorization is already known before the loop body executes. Hoisting the call(s) out of the loop and authorizing each distinct address once turns a linear-in-N cost into a single one-shot dispatch. Loops that legitimately iterate over distinct addresses (the acknowledged edge case from issue #6) can `#[allow(require_auth_in_loop)]` the call site; the lint still reports, so the call stays visible during review.

## How it works

- **Receiver-typed via `cx.typeck_results()`** and matched against the `["soroban_sdk", "Address"]` ADT path, the same pattern used by `redundant_env_clone`, `soroban_storage_in_loop`, and `unnecessary_host_function_call`.
- **Loop detection reuses `get_enclosing_loop_or_multi_call_closure`** via the existing `enclosing_loop` helper, so the new lint correctly excludes calls sitting inside a closure that the loop calls.
- **Method-name match** is made against `REQUIRE_AUTH_METHODS = ["require_auth", "require_auth_for_args"]`. The lint is intentionally **not** included in `SOROBAN_HOST_TYPES`, so the `unnecessary_host_function_call` lint does not double-fire on the same call site.
- **No `depends_on_loop_state` filter**: every `require_auth[_for_args]` call inside a loop body is reported, because legitimate per-iteration cases still benefit from being visible during review.

## Files changed

- `soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs` — declares + registers the new `REQUIRE_AUTH_IN_LOOP` lint and implements `RequireAuthInLoop` (`LateLintPass`).
- `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.rs` — adds fixtures: bad (for / while / loop + `require_auth_for_args`), good (hoisted `require_auth` outside a loop, no auth call at all), legitimate-but-suppressible (`for addr in addrs { addr.require_auth(); }`), and `#[allow(require_auth_in_loop)]` parity fixture.
- `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.stderr` — updated to include the 5 new expected diagnostics (`22 warnings emitted` total).
- `docs/lints/require_auth_in_loop.md` — full reference page (What it does, Why is this bad, Example, Suggested Fix, edge-case acknowledgement).
- `docs/lints/README.md` and `docs/SUMMARY.md` — added new entries; lint now listed under **CPU/Compute**.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — added an Unreleased entry.

## Reference

- Lint reference: [`docs/lints/require_auth_in_loop.md`](docs/lints/require_auth_in_loop.md)
- Cost rationale background: [`docs/cost_rationale.md`](docs/cost_rationale.md)

## Test plan

- [x] New UI fixtures cover the for / while / loop bodies and the `require_auth_for_args` variant.
- [x] Good-pattern fixture (`addr.require_auth()` outside the loop) does not warn.
- [x] Edge-case fixture (`for addr in addrs { addr.require_auth(); }`) still warns, matching the issue requirement that the lint stays visible when iterating over distinct addresses.
- [x] `#[allow(require_auth_in_loop)]` fixture suppresses the warning.
- [x] Existing 4 lints unaffected: pre-existing stderr line numbers (`124 / 131 / 138 / 160 / 178 / 199 / 221 / 227 / 249 / 253 / 261`) are unchanged.

Closes #6
